Brookfield has expanded. Residential streets now reach the eastern boundary, but residents say that services have not developed equally across the area. (13) ______. The solid and dashed lines represent different kinds of information. Brookfield’s experience suggests that assessing development requires both figures and residents’ accounts. A higher urban share describes a population trend, while the blocked entrance reveals a specific access problem. (17) ______. Using both sources can help the council set priorities instead of assuming that expansion alone has improved daily life. Question 13.A. For example, some families can reach a clinic easily but cannot get an appointment after workB. For example, the population figures show precisely which families have difficulty entering their homesC. Collecting accounts of blocked entrances can establish the urban share without population dataB. Recording a higher urban share can establish that residents’ access problems have been resolvedC. Checking local access and reviewing population figures can answer different planning questionsD. Reviewing population figures can establish which entrances are blocked by temporary barriersWrite A, B, C, or D - {#5}
